description: Only results classified after 12th (13th onward) are included. Results classified exactly 12th are excluded.

c.request: Looking only at back-of-the-field results, using 12 as the cutoff on classification order (`positionOrder`), and matching each result to its race: for each race (grouped by race ID and race name), show the race ID, the race name, and the average number of laps completed (`laps`, ignoring missing values). List the 10 races with the highest average first, with any race lacking an average placed last. Only results classified after 12th (13th onward) are included. Results classified exactly 12th are excluded.
c.sql: SELECT r.raceId, r.name, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(NULLIF(res.laps, ''), char(92) || 'N') AS REAL)) AS average_laps FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceId = r.raceId WHERE res.positionOrder > 12 GROUP BY r.raceId, r.name ORDER BY average_laps IS NULL, average_laps DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each race, group results with `positionOrder > 12` by race ID and race name, calculate the average nonmissing `laps`, and return the race ID, race name, and average for the top 10 races ordered by average descending, with missing averages last.
b.sql: SELECT r.raceId, r.name AS race_name, AVG(CASE WHEN res.laps GLOB '[0-9]*' AND res.laps NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*' THEN CAST(res.laps AS REAL) END) AS average_laps FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceId = r.raceId WHERE res.positionOrder > 12 GROUP BY r.raceId, r.name ORDER BY average_laps IS NULL, average_laps DESC LIMIT 10;
b.raw: For each race, group results with `positionOrder > 12` by race ID and race name, calculate the average nonmissing `laps`, and return the race ID, race name, and average for the top 10 races ordered by average descending, with missing averages last.

a.request: Considering only race results whose classification order (`positionOrder`) is greater than 12, each matched to its race, show for each race (grouped by race ID and race name) the race ID, the race name, and the average number of laps completed (`laps`, ignoring missing values). List the 10 races with the highest average first, with any race lacking an average placed last.
a.sql: SELECT r.raceId, r.name, AVG(CASE WHEN res.laps IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(res.laps) NOT IN ('', '\N') THEN CAST(res.laps AS REAL) END) AS average_laps FROM results AS res JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = res.raceId WHERE res.positionOrder > 12 GROUP BY r.raceId, r.name ORDER BY average_laps IS NULL, average_laps DESC, r.raceId LIMIT 10;

d.request: For each race, identified by race ID and race name, calculate the average nonmissing laps completed by results with `positionOrder > 12`, then list the 10 races with the highest averages first and races without an average last.
d.sql: SELECT r.raceId, r.name, AVG(CASE WHEN res.laps IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(res.laps) NOT IN ('', '\N') THEN CAST(res.laps AS REAL) END) AS average_laps FROM races AS r LEFT JOIN results AS res ON res.raceId = r.raceId AND res.positionOrder > 12 GROUP BY r.raceId, r.name ORDER BY average_laps IS NULL, average_laps DESC, r.raceId LIMIT 10
